diagnostic_evidence.quote: An iterative application of the shift-change in Proposition~\ref{prop:Properties}~\ref{itm:shiftChange} and the equivalent notions of distances in Proposition~\ref{prop:Distances} yield for $\delta >0$

One has the shift-change estimate, stating for any $\delta>0$ the existence of a constant $C_\delta < \infty$ such that for all $P,Q\in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $t \geq 0$ \label{itm:shiftChange} \phi_{|P|}(t) &\leq (1+C_\delta) \phi_{|Q|}(t) + \delta\, |F(Q)  - F(P)|^2

issues.failure_explanation: The shift-change estimate (itm:shiftChange) with P = ∇v_h(T_j) and Q = ∇v_h(T_{j+1}) produces the error term δ|F(∇v_h(T_{j+1})) − F(∇v_h(T_j))|² ≍ δφ_{|∇v_h(T_j)|}(|⟦∇_h v_h⟧_{γ_j}|), which involves v_h-gradient jumps. The proof writes this as δφ_{|∇v_h(T_j)|}(|⟦∇_h e_h⟧_{γ_j}|), replacing v_h-jumps with e_h-jumps. Since ⟦∇_h v_h⟧ = ⟦∇_h e_h⟧ + ⟦∇_h u_h⟧, the v_h-jumps are not bounded by e_h-jumps. When chain-face e_h-jumps vanish but v_h-jumps do not (e.g., u_h has the same gradient jumps as v_h at chain faces but e_h = v_h − u_h has a jump at γ), the δ-term is zero while the shift-change error is nonzero, making the inequality in eq:Proofaaassskkkkk- false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must handle the v_h-gradient-jump error terms δ|F(∇v_h(T_{j+1})) − F(∇v_h(T_j))|² arising from the shift-change along the element chain. These terms involve only v_h and cannot be absorbed into the e_h-jump sum on the RHS of eq:Proofaaaassskkk0. Any complete resolution requires either a new argument avoiding the shift-change along chains or a weakened form of eq:Enrichment2 with additional v_h-jump terms that alter the main quasi-optimality guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of eq:Enrichment2 in lem:confComp fails at the shift-change step, leaving eq:Enrichment2 unproven. This propagates to thm:mainResult (quasi-optimality of CR FEM), thm:Apriori (non-conforming a priori estimate), thm:ApproxProperties (interpolation error), and thm:AprioriConf (conforming a priori estimate), all of which rely on eq:Enrichment2.
issues.title: Shift-change error written as e_h-jumps instead of v_h-jumps in enrichment estimate
issues.why_classification: The inequality eq:Proofaaassskkkkk- is itself false (not merely unproven), and correcting the δ-term to v_h-jumps breaks the subsequent absorption step. The resulting extra v_h-gradient-jump terms cannot be bounded by the best-approximation error plus oscillation in the main theorem, so every supported resolution weakens the advertised quasi-optimality guarantee or requires essentially new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For all $Q,P\in \mathbb{R}^d$ one has \label{itm:Udal} $(\phi_{|Q|})^*(|A(Q) - A(P)|) \eqsim \phi_{|Q|}(|Q- P|)

issues.failure_explanation: Property itm:Udal states (φ_{|Q|})* (|A(Q) − A(P)|) ≍ φ_{|Q|}(|Q − P|) with shift |Q|, where Q and P are the two vectors being compared. In eq:Proofaaq34 the two vectors are ∇_h e_h|_{T_+} and ∇_h e_h|_{T_-}, so the correct shift is |∇_h e_h|_{T_+}|. The proof instead uses shift |∇v_h(T_+)| (from the outer function v_h), which is unrelated to |∇_h e_h|_{T_+}|. The equivalence φ_a(|Q−P|) ≍ (φ_a)* (|A(Q)−A(P)|) does not hold uniformly in the shift a: for φ(t) = t³/3 with Q = (2,0), P = (1,0), the ratio φ_a(1)/(φ_a)*(3) equals 4/9 when a = 2 (correct shift) but 25/9 when a = 5, and can be made arbitrarily large or small by varying a. Thus the claimed equivalence is false and the proof of Case 2 in eq:Enrichment2 is invalid.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:confComp (eq:Enrichment2) produces a residual term (φ_{|∇_h v_h|})*(h|div A(∇v)|) involving the convex conjugate of the shifted N-function. The proof of thm:ApproxProperties silently replaces this with φ_{|∇v|}(h|div A(∇v)|), the shifted N-function itself. These are not equivalent: for φ(t) = t^p/p with p = 3 and shift a = |∇v|, the ratio φ_a(t)/(φ_a)*(t) = a² varies with the gradient magnitude and is not bounded by a universal constant. The downstream proof of thm:AprioriConf then applies lem:Oscillation (which bounds (φ)* terms) to bound φ terms, compounding the error. The correct residual is (φ_{|∇v|})*(h|div A(∇v)|), which lem:Oscillation can properly control.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace φ_{|∇v|} with (φ_{|∇v|})* in the residual of thm:ApproxProperties and adjust the proof to use shift-change from |Π_0∇v| to |∇v| for the conjugate function, absorbing the resulting |F(∇v) − F(Π_0∇v)|² correction into the approximation error already present in the bound. The proof of thm:AprioriConf then correctly applies lem:Oscillation to (φ)* terms, yielding the stated bound with osc².
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:ApproxProperties states a residual with φ instead of (φ)*, making the theorem's bound incorrect. The proof of thm:AprioriConf uses this wrong residual and applies lem:Oscillation (which bounds conjugate terms) to bound primal N-function terms, so thm:AprioriConf is also unproven as written.
issues.title: Residual term uses phi instead of phi-conjugate in interpolation error estimate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local change of function (φ to φ*) in the residual of thm:ApproxProperties, with a shift-change step to adjust the shift. This leaves the main quasi-optimality results (thm:mainResult, thm:Apriori, thm:AprioriConf) unchanged in form and guarantee, since the oscillation osc² already uses (φ)*. The residual changes from φ to φ*, which is a comparable N-function-type term.
